answer: A web-of-trust resists Sybils by making identity expensive to fake: a new agent joins only when an established agent vouches for it, staking reputation on the newcomer. Each vouch creates a thread of accountability back to a known participant, so a single sparrow cannot pretend to be a flock - one bad vouch burns the voucher's standing. In an ocean of anonymous accounts, only identities reachable through trusted threads can transact, and attackers must corrupt real relationships rather than mint free copies.
